ideas.name: SunSpotter
ideas.problem: The financial and technical uncertainty renters face when deciding if small-scale, plug-in solar kits are worth the investment due to unpredictable shading and light exposure.
ideas.targetUser: Eco-conscious urban apartment dwellers, ages 22-40, who are tech-savvy and looking to reduce utility costs but do not own their property.
coreFeatures: AR Sunlight Path Visualization
Smart Lux Sensor Integration
Financial Yield & ROI Projection
Automated Kit Sizing & Matching
realDependencies: ARKit/ARCore for spatial mapping
OpenWeatherMap API for historical irradiance data
Geolocation API for sun position calculations
Solar kit product database API
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will bypass real-time AR by using a pre-recorded video loop of a balcony as a background layer. All 'live' data like sunlight intensity and weather will be pulled from a local JSON file containing 'Clear Sky', 'Partly Cloudy', and 'Deep Shadow' profiles. To simulate API communication, a 1.5-second artificial delay will be implemented before displaying results. Real-time sensor data will be replaced by a manual 'Intensity Slider' in the UI to demonstrate how different light levels affect the calculated ROI.

ideas.name: HydroTrace
ideas.niche: Consumer-facing transparency tool for quantifying embedded water usage in groceries and textiles.
ideas.problem: The 'invisible' environmental impact of everyday purchases; consumers lack immediate, actionable data on the water intensity of their specific consumption habits.
ideas.targetUser: Eco-conscious Gen Z and Millennial urban professionals who prioritize sustainable living and already use apps for calorie counting or ethical brand checking.
coreFeatures: AI Receipt Scanner (OCR to identify items)
Visual Water Footprint Dashboard
Smart Eco-Swaps Recommender
Gamified Impact & Saving Milestones
realDependencies: Google Vision API or AWS Textract for OCR
Environmental Impact/LCA Database (e.g., Ecoinvent or Water Footprint Network data)
Product Catalog API (Open Food Facts or UPC lookup services)
Cloud backend (Firebase/Supabase) for user history
ideas.emulationStrategy: The OCR engine will be mocked by matching uploaded image filenames to a local library of pre-defined text strings, accompanied by a 2.5-second 'analyzing' loading state. The LCA database will be simulated via a local JSON lookup table that maps common keywords (e.g., 'Beef', 'Cotton', 'Almonds') to hardcoded liter values. All 'network' requests will use a simulated delay function to mimic real-world latency, and user history will be persisted in LocalStorage to provide the illusion of a live cloud database.

ideas.name: WildStitch
ideas.niche: Residential wildlife corridor connectivity mapping for urban rewilding
ideas.problem: Urban habitat fragmentation prevents pollinators and migratory birds from moving through residential areas, creating isolated 'biological islands' that threaten local biodiversity.
ideas.targetUser: Eco-conscious suburban homeowners, members of local rewilding groups, and urban gardeners (ages 30-65) looking to turn individual gardens into a coordinated ecological network.
coreFeatures: Native Plant Logger with Photo ID
Real-time Connectivity Heatmap
Gap-Filling Recommendations
Community Wildlife Sightings Log
realDependencies: Mapbox GL JS for high-resolution spatial visualization
iNaturalist API for botanical and species identification
Google Geocoding API for precise residential location mapping
Firebase Realtime Database for live community updates
ideas.emulationStrategy: The map will be emulated using a local Leaflet.js instance with a static satellite imagery layer and a pre-defined GeoJSON file containing hardcoded 'user garden' coordinates in a single neighborhood. The Plant ID feature will use a local JSON dictionary of 50 common native species; when a user 'uploads' a photo, the app will trigger a 2.5-second 'analyzing' loading spinner followed by a successful match from the dictionary. The Connectivity Heatmap will be simulated by calculating the distance between the hardcoded GeoJSON points and rendering translucent green polygons or 'links' between points that fall within a 50-meter threshold. All community updates and sightings will be simulated by injecting new objects into the local application state using a randomized delay between 500ms and 2000ms to mimic real-world network latency.

ideas.name: VeriScope
ideas.niche: B2B Greenwashing Risk Mitigation & Procurement Compliance
ideas.problem: Procurement teams risk legal penalties and reputational damage by purchasing from suppliers making unsubstantiated or vague environmental claims that lack verifiable third-party certification.
ideas.targetUser: Procurement Managers, ESG Compliance Officers, and Supply Chain Auditors at enterprise-level companies operating under strict regulatory frameworks like the EU Green Claims Directive.
coreFeatures: Semantic Claim Analyzer: Uses NLP to extract specific environmental claims from supplier marketing text or uploaded PDF documents.
Cross-Reference Engine: Automates the matching of extracted claims against a global database of accredited environmental certifications (e.g., FSC, ISO, Fairtrade).
Greenwash Risk Index: A dynamic scoring system (0-100) that flags 'vague', 'unsupported', or 'high-risk' claims based on certification gaps.
Compliance Audit Trail: Generates timestamped, exportable verification reports for use in regulatory filings and internal audits.
realDependencies: NLP/LLM API (e.g., OpenAI GPT-4) for semantic claim extraction
Certification Registry APIs (e.g., FSC, Rainforest Alliance, or EcoVadis)
OCR Services (e.g., AWS Textract) for reading physical certificate scans
ESG Intelligence Data Feeds (e.g., MSCI or CDP)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will use a local 'Mock Registry' JSON file containing pre-defined certifications and supplier profiles. The 'Semantic Analyzer' will simulate AI logic using a keyword-weighting script (e.g., if the input contains 'Carbon Neutral' but lacks 'Gold Standard' in the mock database, it triggers a 'High Risk' flag). A 'Latency Wrapper' will be applied to all data fetches, introducing random delays between 1.5 and 3 seconds to simulate real-world API calls, and a 'Mock Error Injector' will occasionally return 500-series errors to demonstrate the UI's error-handling capabilities.

ideas.name: SwiftSpace
ideas.niche: Hyperlocal micro-logistics via underutilized vehicle capacity
ideas.problem: Prohibitive last-mile delivery costs and high carbon footprints for small businesses due to inefficient, single-purpose courier routing and redundant vehicle trips.
ideas.targetUser: Urban boutique retailers/artisans needing affordable local shipping and daily commuters or gig workers seeking supplemental income by utilizing existing trunk/seat space.
coreFeatures: Smart Capacity Matching: An algorithm that matches package dimensions and weight to the specific available volume of a driver's vehicle.
Route Overlay Engine: Integrates delivery waypoints into a driver's existing GPS route to minimize detours and maximize efficiency.
Eco-Impact Dashboard: A real-time tracker showing CO2 emissions saved compared to traditional courier services for both merchants and drivers.
QR-Verified Handshake: A secure, contact-free verification system using mobile QR scanning for both pickup and successful drop-off.
realDependencies: Google Maps Platform (Directions and Distance Matrix API for routing)
Stripe (For automated split-payments between the platform and drivers)
Twilio (For real-time SMS arrival and delivery status updates)
Firebase Realtime Database (For live geospatial tracking of drivers)
ideas.emulationStrategy: The demo will utilize a 'MockService' layer to intercept all asynchronous calls. Instead of real Google Maps, the app will use a local GeoJSON file containing predefined paths to animate driver icons along specific routes. To simulate network latency, every API call will be wrapped in a Promise that resolves after a randomized delay of 1000ms to 3500ms. 'Driver Discovery' will return mock JSON payloads containing nearby driver objects with randomized 'currentLocation' coordinates. Driver movement will be emulated via a setInterval loop that incrementally updates these coordinates, creating a realistic moving-vehicle effect on the UI without actual GPS hardware.
